comment: SPR-I.4.1 golden takes for the judge. Every case is over | Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7 | % | in C, 4/4, 120 bpm (a beat is 500 ms, a bar 2000 ms), t_ms 0 being the downbeat of bar 1 after the count-in. Dm7 is D F A C with F and C the guide tones and D Dorian its first-choice scale; G7 is G B D F over G Mixolydian; Cmaj7 is C E G B over C Major. These are hand-checked musical judgements: change one only with a reason and a judge_version bump.

cases.name: every note a chord tone, on the beat: full marks, right on the beat
a scale tone and an outside note over Dm7, each called what it is
cases.why: E is in D Dorian but not in Dm7; Eb is in neither, and the A that follows it is not the chord tone a semitone away, so it is not an approach

cases.name: the same notes scored on chord tones on the beat give half marks
an outside note that steps into a chord tone within a beat is an approach note
cases.why: Eb is outside Dm7 and D Dorian, a semitone below D, and D lands 500 ms later

cases.name: an outside note followed by the chord tone too late is only outside
cases.why: D comes 600 ms after the Eb, more than the beat an approach is allowed

cases.name: an outside note followed by a chord tone that is not its neighbour is only outside
a note just before the chord change is judged against the chord it anticipates
cases.why: B at 1900 is 100 ms before G7, inside the half-beat look-ahead, so it is G7's third; B at 1700 is still over Dm7, where it is a Dorian scale tone

cases.name: the fourth bar repeats the third, and the loop comes round to Dm7 again
notes a steady 30 ms late are told so in words, and the offset puts it right
notes early are rushing
cases.why: the first note is before t 0 but inside half a beat of it, so it is a note on beat 1, not a count-in note

cases.name: a note more than a tenth of a beat off is outside the tolerance
cases.why: the tolerance at 120 bpm is 50 ms; 80 ms late is outside it

cases.name: free play has metrics and no score
chord tones on the named beats only count the notes on those beats
cases.why: the Ebs on beats 2 and 4 are outside, but only beats 1 and 3 are asked about

cases.name: a note too far from any named beat is not a note on that beat
cases.why: the A at 250 ms sits between beats 1 and 2, so it is nobody's beat and is not counted either way

cases.name: notes during the count-in are not judged, and the take still scores
no notes at all is nought, not a crash
an eighth note is on the eighth grid and off the beat grid
cases.why: on the beat grid the second note is 250 ms from both beats, and the earlier one is taken, so it reads 250 late; the mean over both notes is 125

cases.name: a swung off-beat is on time on the swung grid and late on the straight one
cases.why: at 0.67 the off-beat lands 335 ms into the beat; the straight eighth is at 250, so the note is 85 late there and the mean over both notes is 42.5, rounded up
